subject: general
question: Which of the following statements regarding the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and State legislatures is **correct**?

options.text: The State legislature can legislate on matters enumerated in the Union List
The Union legislature can legislate on matters in the Concurrent List only with State approval
The Union Government can issue directions to the States under Article 256
The Union and States have equal powers on matters in the Union List

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Union Government can issue directions to the States under Article 256**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 256 of the Indian Constitution states that the executive power of every state is to be exercised in a way that ensures compliance with the laws made by the Parliament.
 
• The Union Government has the authority to issue directions to the states to ensure the implementation of such laws.
 
• This provision ensures the supremacy of parliamentary laws over state laws in case of conflict.
 
• Such directions issued by the Union are binding on the states, and non-compliance may result in consequences under Article 356 (President’s Rule).
 
• This mechanism ensures the cohesive functioning of the federal structure in India and maintains the unity and integrity of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Legislature (Parliament)**

 
 
• Composition: President, Lok Sabha (House of the People), and Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• Powers: Exclusive power over Union List, concurrent power over Concurrent List, with overriding power over states.
 
• Rajya Sabha: Indirectly elected, permanent house (not dissolved), one-third members retire every two years, 12 nominated members for arts/science.
 
• Lok Sabha: Directly elected, represents the people. 
 
 
 
• **State Legislature**
 
 
• Composition: Varies; some bicameral (Assembly & Council), most unicameral (Assembly only).
 
• Powers: Exclusive power over State List, concurrent power over Concurrent List.
 
• Legislative Council (Upper House): Indirectly elected members from local authorities, graduates, teachers, MLAs, and nominated by Governor; permanent house, not dissolved, one-third retire every two years.
 
• Legislative Assembly (Lower House): Directly elected by people, members 40-500.
